quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
When parked on a level roadway with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
questions.explanation: When waiting to turn left, keep your wheels straight. A car hitting you from behind will not push you into oncoming traffic. On hills, turn your wheels so your car won't roll into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: Drivers must obey instructions from:

options.text: Other drivers with broken-down vehicles on the road.

questions.explanation: Drivers must obey flaggers and their signals. Flaggers are there to keep drivers and workers safe.

questions.question: Construction zone signs are usually:

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red colors.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow colors.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black colors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black colors.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. They appear on the right side of the road, or on both sides on divided highways.

questions.question: When are you allowed to double park?
questions.explanation: Double parking is illegal.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What should you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car or property, you must leave a note with your name, phone number, and address attached to the damaged vehicle or property.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check for other vehicles in the same lane.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, make sure no vehicles are in your way. Check your mirrors and blind spots. Always use your turn signal to warn other drivers.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This orange sign warns that roadwork is coming. Stay alert for temporary traffic controls in work zones.

questions.question: When should you drive on the shoulder to pass a car?

options.text: If the car ahead is turning left.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver won't expect you there and may pull onto the road.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at accidents or unusual events:
questions.explanation: Avoid slowing down to look at accidents or unusual events. This creates traffic congestion.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:
questions.explanation: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming traffic. Only turn when it is safe and will not affect oncoming cars.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Dangerous if you have a helper.

questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Be extra careful when backing up.

questions.question: If you drive with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of 0.10 percent, you are ____ times more likely to cause an accident than when sober.
questions.explanation: Alcohol greatly increases crash risk. A driver with a BAC of 0.10 percent is seven times more likely to crash than a sober driver. At 0.15 percent BAC, the risk is 25 times higher. At 0.17 percent BAC, the risk is 50 times higher.

questions.question: Driving slower than other traffic is:

options.text: A good idea if the weather is bad.
Appropriate if you don't know the speed limit.
Often dangerous because frustrated drivers may try to pass you in unsafe ways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often dangerous because frustrated drivers may try to pass you in unsafe ways.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. Drivers behind you may become impatient and try risky passing moves.

questions.question: When rain or fog reduces visibility, drivers should use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off water and rain, making visibility worse for you and other drivers.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. To prevent it in wet weather, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down when the pavement is wet to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: Broken yellow lines on roads are used to:

options.text: Separate lanes of traffic going the same direction.
Separate lanes of traffic going opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Separate lanes of traffic going opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. Broken lines mean you can pass when it is safe.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection. It is unsafe and illegal to turn right where this sign is posted.

questions.question: You are driving behind a large truck on the freeway. You should drive:

options.text: Close behind the truck in bad weather so you can see farther ahead.
Farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
Only one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely behind a truck, the driver cannot see you. Stay far enough back so you can see the truck's side mirrors. Tailgating is dangerous because you lose time to react if the truck stops suddenly.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance behind a large vehicle:

options.text: So you can see around the sides of the vehicle.
Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before passing.
Because following too closely will trap you in the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you can see around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Truck, bus, and van drivers cannot see you if you drive directly behind them. Increase your distance behind large vehicles so you can see around them and see the road ahead.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign means:
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of hazards or special conditions ahead. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: It means the same thing as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
It means the same thing as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. You must yield to traffic and pedestrians before moving forward. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn in the direction shown by the arrow. In this case, right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: A police officer tells you to go through a red light without stopping. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to turn green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: Police officers directing traffic have authority over traffic signals and signs. Always follow a police officer's directions.

questions.question: A child on a bicycle is near your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Assume the child has full control of the bicycle.

questions.explanation: Children on bicycles are unpredictable. They often make sudden changes in direction without warning. Children and bicycles are small and hard to see, so stay alert.

questions.question: Which vehicle is NOT required to stop at a railroad crossing?
questions.explanation: School and church buses must always stop at railroad crossings. Taxis and vehicles carrying passengers for hire must also stop. Farm trucks hauling produce are not in these required categories.

questions.question: How far should your body be from the steering wheel when sitting upright?
questions.explanation: Sit 10 to 12 inches away from the steering wheel. This distance helps protect your head and neck in a crash.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other roads. They also thaw out later than the rest of the road. Be cautious on bridges in cold weather.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Slow down and use low beam headlights.
Slow down and use high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. If you cannot see ahead, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: Your vehicle starts to skid. What should you do?
questions.explanation: When your vehicle skids, release the gas or brake pedal to regain balance. Steer in the direction of the skid to get control back.

questions.question: Why is it more dangerous to drive at night than during the day?

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead as during the day. Oncoming headlights also cause glare. Always use headlights and drive carefully in the dark.
